title: No Forge-owned observation/debug execution contract
expected_semantics: Debug observation executes through Forge-owned confinement with artifact ownership, deadlines, bounded output, execution identity, and provenance, like any other family execution.
actual_behavior_limitation: The debugger executes `mncs observe/call` through owned subprocesses with explicit cwd/timeout/env; Forge consumes the debugger through the JSONL api/provider boundary but cannot submit or own observation-mode work.
why_capability_matters: Two execution owners (Forge for workflows, debugger for observation) duplicate confinement, deadline, and provenance logic and risk divergence.
current_workaround: Debugger-side execution stays explicit and bounded (cwd, timeout, sanitized env, recorded libraries); Forge drives witness-mode break/watch/inspect/trace/why/replay/minimize through the api without new processes.

host_language_code_required.why: Process execution is inherently host-bound until a Forge observation contract exists.

proposed_primitive_or_semantic_direction: A small Forge observation-mode execution contract (submit program+request+capture policy, receive bounded observation artifact with Forge execution identity) that record/import-test can target with an explicit executor flag.
alternatives_considered: shell-only Forge steps calling the CLI (no typed contract)
resolution_criteria: A record-equivalent observation can be submitted through Forge with Forge-owned identity and provenance, chosen explicitly per invocation.
